headline: Easy-run HR is holding low into a third block while volume stays nearly doubled and strength frequency hasn't slipped.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The aerobic efficiency story has now stabilised rather than just appeared — comparable easy efforts continue to sit at a lower heart rate than the prior period, and this is happening while your running load is still carried near the top of your recent range. That combination is the meaningful part: adaptation that persists under sustained volume is more trustworthy than a single good block, and it suggests the elevated load is being absorbed rather than merely tolerated.

Equally worth noting is that strength frequency has held flat rather than dropping off, which is the usual casualty when running volume jumps this sharply. Keeping both channels running simultaneously is exactly the hybrid balance you're aiming for, and it means the volume increase isn't costing you elsewhere.

With the St. Olavsleden multi-day effort roughly a month out, this consolidation of aerobic durability at higher load is well-timed — but the cleaner confirmation still comes if easy paces drift back toward previous levels while HR stays down. Right now the evidence supports genuine efficiency gain; keep watching whether the pace side of the trade-off follows.
watch_items: Watch whether easy paces begin creeping back up while HR stays low — that's the stronger confirmation of the adaptation.
Keep an eye on strength frequency holding as running load stays elevated into the pre-event month.
Note whether durability and time-on-feet feel steady as St. Olavsleden approaches, given the pack-carry demands ahead.
As sleep tracking accumulates, watch for any link between low-score nights and next-day aerobic HR.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 177 km vs 92 km prior block (+92%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 142 bpm vs 155 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 9 vs 6 runs)
▲ Zone 2: 211 min vs 180-240 min/week target (117% of minimum); grey zone (Z3+Z4): 0.3%
